abhiseka.gloss: consecration by sprinkling: that by which one is installed in office.
abhiseka.name: Abhiṣeka

abhyasa.gloss: repetition — that by which what was once understood becomes one’s own. For Abhinavagupta it is not the building of a skill, but the returning of attention to the same place.
abhyasa.name: Abhyāsa

adhvan.gloss: path: a way of breaking the universe into a series through which it is traversed. There are six paths, three on the side of the word and three on the side of the thing.
adhvan.name: Adhvan

agama.gloss: “that which has come” — revelation received from the Lord, not deduced by the mind.
agama.name: Āgama

ahankara.gloss: the “I-maker”: that by which an impersonal impression becomes “mine.”
ahankara.name: Ahaṅkāra

ahnika.gloss: “daily” — a chapter: as much as is examined in one day. There are thirty-seven of them.
ahnika.name: Āhnika

ajnana.gloss: ignorance — not a lack of information, but incomplete knowledge taken as complete. Of two kinds: that seated in the being and that seated in the mind.
ajnana.name: Ajñāna

ananda.gloss: bliss — not pleasure, but the fullness of Consciousness content with itself.
ananda.name: Ānanda

anava.gloss: the path of the limited being: reliance on body, breath, sound, and object.
anava.name: Āṇava

anda.gloss: "egg"—the shell of the universe. There are four of them, nested one inside another: of the earth, of nature, of māyā, and of Power.
anda.name: Aṇḍa

angula.gloss: finger as a measure of length: by it the path of breath is measured.
angula.name: Aṅgula

anupaya.gloss: “without means” — not a path, but its absence: recognition without a single step.
anupaya.name: Anupāya

anuttara.gloss: “that above which there is nothing”: the Supreme Reality from which everything proceeds and in which everything rests.
anuttara.name: Anuttara

apana.gloss: descending current of breath, the pair to prāṇa.
apana.name: Apāna

arghapatra.gloss: offering bowl: in it what the rite offers is mixed, and from it one also partakes.
arghapatra.name: Arghapātra

astra.gloss: "weapon" — the mantra by which the place is purified and obstruction warded off. One of the limb-mantras, on a par with the heart and the head.
astra.name: Astra

avastha.gloss: state: waking, dreaming sleep, deep sleep — and the fourth, Turya, which is not beside them but through them.
avastha.name: Avasthā

avesha.gloss: entry, being possessed: the state when that to which one is devoted enters into a person.
avesha.name: Āveśa

bhairava.gloss: the name of the Supreme Lord in Trika: He who holds the universe, bears it, and draws it back in. Not a “terrifying deity,” but the fullness of Consciousness.
bhairava.name: Bhairava

bhavana.gloss: cultivation: not imagination, but holding the truth until it becomes evident.
bhavana.name: Bhāvanā

bheda.gloss: difference, separateness — that by which the bonds are held. 231 notes.
bheda.name: Bheda

bhoga.gloss: tasting, enjoyment. In Trika it is not opposed to liberation: the path leads to both.
bhoga.name: Bhoga

bhuvana.gloss: world, inhabited region; there are a hundred and eighteen of them, and they are the most fractional portion of the path on the side of the thing.
bhuvana.name: Bhuvana

bija.gloss: seed — a one-syllable mantra, from which a whole grows.
bija.name: Bīja

bindu.gloss: point, drop: compressed into one, from which the many unfolds.
bindu.name: Bindu

bodha.gloss: awakening, discernment — Consciousness taken as that which understands.
bodha.name: Bodha

buddhi.gloss: the discriminating faculty: that which decides “this is that.”
buddhi.name: Buddhi

cakra.gloss: wheel: both a center in the body, and a circle of deities, and an assembly of initiates. Abhinavagupta uses all three senses.
cakra.name: Cakra

camatkara.gloss: the rapture of recognition — a flash in which Consciousness tastes itself.
camatkara.name: Camatkāra

cit.gloss: Consciousness as such, the pure capacity to shine. Everything is composed of it: cinmaya — “consisting of Consciousness.”
cit.name: Cit

citta.gloss: the consciousness of an individual person — that which can be defiled and which is purified.
citta.name: Citta

dana.gloss: giving — and that which is given: one of the actions by which the rite is sustained.
dana.name: Dāna

deha.gloss: body. In the Tantrāloka it is not an obstacle but the place where everything happens.
deha.name: Deha

devata.gloss: deity — and the circle of deities (devatā-cakra), whom in the rite one worships as powers of one's own Consciousness, not as alien persons.
devata.name: Devatā

devi.gloss: the Goddess — God’s Power, taken as His own inseparable side; in the Tantrāloka she is also the interlocutor who asks questions.
devi.name: Devī

dharana.gloss: concentration: binding consciousness to a single place.
dharana.name: Dhāraṇā

dhyana.gloss: contemplation — holding an image until it becomes itself.
dhyana.name: Dhyāna

diksa.gloss: initiation: the rite by which the teacher burns away the bonds of the pupil. The greater part of the treatise is devoted to it.
diksa.name: Dīkṣā

dvadashanta.gloss: “end of twelve” — the point twelve fingers from the body or from the palate, where breath ends and begins.
dvadashanta.name: Dvādaśānta

guna.gloss: three threads from which nature is woven: sattva, rajas, tamas.
guna.name: Guṇa

guru.gloss: teacher. For Abhinavagupta he is not a mentor but one through whom the Power acts.
guru.name: Guru

homa.gloss: libation into the fire; for Abhinavagupta what is burnt is not butter but difference.
homa.name: Homa

hrdaya.gloss: Heart — not an organ but a center: that to which everything converges and from which everything issues.
hrdaya.name: Hṛdaya

iccha.gloss: will, desire — the first of the three Powers: with it every manifestation begins.
iccha.name: Icchā

indriya.gloss: instrument: five senses and five actions. Not the eye itself, but that by which one sees.
indriya.name: Indriya

ishvara.gloss: the fourth tattva — and at the same time simply “the Lord.” Here the emphasis is already on “this”: the universe is seen clearly, and the “I” holds it.
ishvara.name: Īśvara

jnana.gloss: knowledge — the second Power: that in which desire sees what it wants.
jnana.name: Jñāna

kala.gloss: portion, part—the largest division of the path: five kalās into which the whole universe is broken. Not to be confused with kāla, time.
kala.name: Kalā

kalatime.gloss: time—both as a covering that cuts eternity down to "now," and as the One who devours. Written with a long "ā," unlike the portion kalā.
kalatime.name: Kāla (time)

kancuka.gloss: covering: five sheaths by which māyā cuts the boundless down to "so much"—kalā, vidyā, rāga, kāla-time, niyati.
kancuka.name: Kañcuka

karma.gloss: deed — and its consequence. For Abhinavagupta, not fate, but a trace that is erased by initiation.
karma.name: Karma

kaula.gloss: that which pertains to the Kula: the tradition in which nothing is cast away as impure.
kaula.name: Kaula

krama.gloss: succession, sequence — and at the same time the name of a school. 245 notes: the Tantrāloka lays out almost everything by stages.
krama.name: Krama

kriya.gloss: action — the third Power: knowledge become deed.
kriya.name: Kriyā

kula.gloss: clan, family — and at the same time a totality: the body, the Power, the assembly of the initiated.
kula.name: Kula

kumbha.gloss: vessel of water placed at the centre of the rite, in which the deity is present just as in the image.
kumbha.name: Kumbha

linga.gloss: sign — both the object of worship and the mark by which one recognises.
linga.name: Liṅga

madhya.gloss: middle — both the place between the two breaths, and that state which one enters through any interval.
madhya.name: Madhya

madhyama.gloss: “middle” — the third: words are already separate, but sound within.
madhyama.name: Madhyamā

maheshvara.gloss: the Great Lord. The word stands both as a name and as an indication that this lordship depends on nothing.
maheshvara.name: Maheśvara

mala.gloss: dirt, stain: that by which consciousness is closed off from itself. There are three, and in the translation they are named in Russian: ānava — “I am incomplete,” from it the boundless becomes a point; māyiya — “this is not I,” the world becomes alien and separate; karma — “I am the doer,” hence the deed, the trace, and new birth.
mala.name: Mala

malini.gloss: “she who wears a garland” — a sound series in reverse order, and the name of the tantra on which the treatise relies most heavily.
malini.name: Mālinī

manas.gloss: the mind: that which assembles impressions into an image.
manas.name: Manas

mandala.gloss: circle, diagram: the universe laid out on a plane, into which the pupil is led.
mandala.name: Maṇḍala

mantra.gloss: a word by which one acts. For Abhinavagupta, the power of a mantra lies not in sound, but in Consciousness, which recognises itself through it.
mantra.name: Mantra

matrka.gloss: “mother” — the entire sound series as the mother of every word and every knowledge.
matrka.name: Mātṛkā

maya.gloss: the Power by which the Lord conceals Himself and manifests the world as separate. Not deception, but measure: the sixth tattva.
maya.name: Māyā

moksa.gloss: liberation — is not a departure from the world, but the recognition that there was no bondage.
moksa.name: Mokṣa

mudra.gloss: seal: a position of body or consciousness by which a state is fixed.
mudra.name: Mudrā

mukti.gloss: the same liberation in other words; more often where the state is concerned.
mukti.name: Mukti

murti.gloss: image, statue — one of the places where the rite is performed, on a par with the vessel, the fire, and one's own body.
murti.name: Mūrti

nada.gloss: hum, undifferentiated sounding, from which the sounds of speech are distinguished.
nada.name: Nāda

nadi.gloss: channel along which breath moves; there are three main ones.
nadi.name: Nāḍī

naimittika.gloss: occasional rite — as opposed to nitya, the daily one: the occasion may be a festival, a death, or simply an unlooked-for joy.
naimittika.name: Naimittika

nyasa.gloss: placement: the arrangement of mantras over the body, by which the body is made the body of the deity.
nyasa.name: Nyāsa

pada.gloss: word as a unit of the path—and generally "place, state."
pada.name: Pada

paramarsha.gloss: “grasping”: that very act by which Consciousness touches itself and says “I.” Not a thought about oneself, but the very self-holding from which both the sounds of speech and the world emerge.
paramarsha.name: Parāmarśa

pasha.gloss: noose, bond — the general name for everything that holds a being bound.
pasha.name: Pāśa

pashu.gloss: cattle — the bound being: the same Consciousness, but having forgotten itself.
pashu.name: Paśu

pashyanti.gloss: “seeing” — the second stage: the meaning is seen whole, but not yet broken into words.
pashyanti.name: Paśyantī

pavitraka.gloss: consecrated cord — and the rite by which it is offered: with it, once a year, all that is unfinished and omitted is covered. The last chapter is devoted to it.
pavitraka.name: Pavitraka

phala.gloss: fruit: that for the sake of which one acts — and that which comes out of what is done.
phala.name: Phala

prakasha.gloss: Light — that side of Reality by which it manifests. Without it nothing would be; without a response it would not know that it shines.
prakasha.name: Prakāśa

prakrti.gloss: nature—that from which everything material is made; the thirteenth tattva.
prakrti.name: Prakṛti

pramana.gloss: means of cognition — that by which the knower takes the knowable.
pramana.name: Pramāṇa

pramatr.gloss: the knower — the one for whom something exists. Its levels are seven, from Śiva to the bound being.
pramatr.name: Pramātṛ

prameya.gloss: the knowable — that which is taken.
prameya.name: Prameya

prana.gloss: breath-life — and its ascending current in particular.
prana.name: Prāṇa

pratibimba.gloss: reflection. The third chapter rests on it: the world stands in Consciousness as a reflection in a mirror — and the original from which it is taken does not exist at all.
pratibimba.name: Pratibimba

prayashcitta.gloss: expiation: that by which a broken rule or an unfinished rite is set right.
prayashcitta.name: Prāyaścitta

purnata.gloss: fullness — a state in which there is nothing to add and nothing to desire.
purnata.name: Pūrṇatā

purusa.gloss: limited being: Consciousness that has forgotten its boundlessness.
purusa.name: Puruṣa

rasa.gloss: juice, taste: that by which a thing is grasped from within, not examined from without. Consciousness takes the world “with the juice of its own response.”
rasa.name: Rasa

sadashiva.gloss: the third tattva: the stage where “I am this” still sounds with the emphasis on “I.”
sadashiva.name: Sadāśiva

sakala.gloss: “with parts” — the bound being who has all three stains. Above him is pralayākala, who lacks the māyic one, and vijñānākala, who has only the first remaining.
sakala.name: Sakala

samavesha.gloss: full entry — that for the sake of which all means are set up.
samavesha.name: Samāveśa

samaya.gloss: the rule of the initiated: the precepts accepted together with the first initiation. Samayin — one who keeps them.
samaya.name: Samaya

samsara.gloss: cycle of births — and at the same time all of ordinary life.
samsara.name: Saṁsāra

samskara.gloss: trace left by a deed; and the rite by which it is set right.
samskara.name: Saṁskāra

samvid.gloss: Consciousness — not “my consciousness,” but that one by which anything at all is.
samvid.name: Saṁvid

shabda.gloss: sound, word — what is heard, as opposed to what it means.
shabda.name: Śabda

shakta.gloss: the path of Power: working with thought — displacing bad discriminative thought with pure thought.
shakta.name: Śākta

shakti.gloss: The Power of God, His I-Consciousness: the same Reality taken as will and movement. Three hundred annotations — the second most frequent word of the treatise.
shakti.name: Śakti

shaktipata.gloss: descent of Power: the grace by which the Lord reveals Himself. Without it initiation has no force.
shaktipata.name: Śaktipāta

shambhava.gloss: the path of Śambhu: entry by will alone, without reliance on thought or breath.
shambhava.name: Śāmbhava

shastra.gloss: scripture, instruction. Note 171: “Tantrāloka” continuously refers to other books of the tradition.
shastra.name: Śāstra

shisya.gloss: pupil — the one who is initiated.
shisya.name: Śiṣya

shiva.gloss: God as the resting side of Reality — the Light of Consciousness, not different from His own Power. The most frequent word of the treatise: 376 occurrences.
shiva.name: Śiva

shrikantha.gloss: “fair-throated” — Śiva from whom the teaching’s transmission is traced in the treatise.
shrikantha.name: Śrīkaṇṭha

shunya.gloss: emptiness — a state in which there is nothing knowable. Not the goal: beyond it opens that for which even emptiness was an object.
shunya.name: Śūnya

siddhi.gloss: perfection, superpower — and at the same time "that which has come true."
siddhi.name: Siddhi

spanda.gloss: quiver: not movement in space, but that stirring within Consciousness without which it would manifest nothing.
spanda.name: Spanda

sphuratta.gloss: flashing, shimmering — the same stirring taken as radiance.
sphuratta.name: Sphurattā

srsti.gloss: manifestation, emission—the first of the five acts of the Lord.
srsti.name: Sṛṣṭi

sthandila.gloss: level ground on which the rite is performed — a place become a throne.
sthandila.name: Sthaṇḍila

svarupa.gloss: one's own essential nature — that which a being has always been.
svarupa.name: Svartipa

svatantrya.gloss: Absolute Freedom — that which makes the Lord the Lord: the unconstrained possibility to manifest or not to manifest.
svatantrya.name: Svātantrya

tanmatra.gloss: "only that": the subtle basis of an element—sound, touch, color, taste, smell, taken by themselves, before any thing.
tanmatra.name: Tanmātra

tantra.gloss: book of revelation — and at the same time “the warp of the fabric”: that by which everything is woven together.
tantra.name: Tantra

tarka.gloss: reasoning. Of all the parts of yoga, Abhinavagupta places it first: correct reasoning (sattarka) itself dismantles the division that neither posture nor breath retention can take on.
tarka.name: Tarka

tarpana.gloss: satisfying: the libation by which the deities of the circle are nourished — and through them, oneself.
tarpana.name: Tarpaṇa

tattva.gloss: beginning, level of Reality; there are thirty-six of them—from Śiva down to the earth. The most frequent concept of the treatise after Śiva: 323 annotations.
tattva.name: Tattva

trika.gloss: “triad” — the name of the school itself: Śiva, Śakti, and the bound being, taken as one.
trika.name: Trika

turya.gloss: the Fourth — the state beyond waking, dreaming sleep, and dreamless sleep.
turya.name: Turya

ucchara.gloss: rising — a prolonged utterance by which consciousness is led upward along the central channel.
ucchara.name: Ucchāra

udana.gloss: current going upward along the central channel: the one that raises into Turīya.
udana.name: Udāna

upaya.gloss: means: the way by which a being comes to itself. Abhinavagupta has four of them, and the entire treatise is arranged according to them.
upaya.name: Upāya

vac.gloss: Speech — not sound, but that by which anything at all can be named and therefore be. It has four stages: the highest (parā), paśyantī, madhyamā and vaikharī.
vac.name: Vāc

varga.gloss: row — a group of five consonants of one place of articulation (ka-varga, ca-varga). By them the whole alphabet is laid out, and by the alphabet — the whole world.
varga.name: Varga

varna.gloss: sound of speech, letter—the smallest portion of the path on the side of the word.
varna.name: Varṇa

vasana.gloss: habit, accumulated inclination — and at the same time “fragrance.”
vasana.name: Vāsanā

vedya.gloss: the same knowable under another word; the pair to vedaka.
vedya.name: Vedya

vidya.gloss: knowledge—and that tattva (śuddhavidyā), on which "I" and "this" still hold together; below māyā it becomes the narrow knowledge of a single person.
vidya.name: Vidyā

vikalpa.gloss: discriminating thought: that which cuts the one into “this” and “not this.”
vikalpa.name: Vikalpa

vimarsha.gloss: response, the self-awareness of Light: “this is I.” The pair to prakāśa, and the whole system rests on their being one.
vimarsha.name: Vimarśa

vira.gloss: "hero" — a participant in the Kaula rite: one able to take it up without fear and without being seduced.
vira.name: Vīra

visarga.gloss: “emission”: that by which Fullness pours the world out of itself, losing nothing. It is also the sign ḥ — two dots with which the sound series ends.
visarga.name: Visarga

vishranti.gloss: rest — not repose after work, but that into which every movement comes and in which it holds. “Resting in oneself” is bliss itself.
vishranti.name: Viśrānti

vishva.gloss: universe as a whole—everything that exists, taken in a single glance.
vishva.name: Viśva

vrata.gloss: vow — an accepted restriction by which one holds oneself to what has been begun.
vrata.name: Vrata

yaga.gloss: sacrifice, service — the rite as a whole.
yaga.name: Yāga

yoga.gloss: union — and the way to achieve it.
yoga.name: Yoga
